finding.title: Buffer overflow in recvfrom function
finding.trigger: Sending a packet larger than sizeof(uint32_t)
finding.assumptions: The client can send packets larger than the expected size of uint32_t.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
Checked that recvfrom receives at most the buffer size (sizeof(uint32_t)=4). In UDP, if a datagram is larger than the supplied buffer, the excess data is discarded and recvfrom returns the truncated size. Thus no buffer overflow can occur; the input is limited by the buffer argument. No neutralising checks needed as the source is already bounded by the call.
Evidence lines: 41

finding.title: OS command injection via user input
finding.trigger: Sending a crafted input that triggers an OS command
finding.assumptions: The user input is not properly sanitized before being used.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
1) Examined the code for any system or exec family calls; none found.
2) The only sink highlighted (sendto) is a network transmission function that merely sends raw bytes; it does not interpret or execute them as commands.
3) The user input is read as a hexadecimal integer via scanf("%x", &number). This input is stored in a uint32_t variable and then sent unchanged (after byte‑order conversion). There is no path from this input to any OS command execution primitive.
4) No sanitization step is required for command injection because the data is not passed to a command interpreter.

finding.title: Integer overflow in recvfrom function
finding.trigger: Sending a packet with a large size
finding.assumptions: The client can send packets with a size that causes integer overflow.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the recvfrom call at line 41: the length argument is a compile‑time constant sizeof(uint32_t) (4). Since size_t is unsigned and the constant is small, there is no path for an integer overflow from client input. The source of data (client packet) cannot influence the length parameter. Therefore the reported overflow cannot occur.
